message.content: In Christian tradition, the figure most often regarded as central to the faith is Jesus Christ. Christians believe that Jesus is the fulfillment of the prophetic tradition that began with figures such as Moses, Isaiah, and Jeremiah, and that He is the ultimate revelation of God’s will to humanity. At the same time, many Christians also hold the prophets of the Hebrew Bible—especially Moses, who delivered the Law, and Isaiah, whose writings anticipate the coming of the Messiah—in high regard for their foundational role in shaping the theological and moral framework of the faith. Thus, while Jesus is typically seen as the pivotal figure, the prophets of the Old Testament are also considered highly significant within Christian theology.
